results.name: Star Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides, maintaining an upright posture.
Bend your knees slightly and lower into a half-squat position to prepare for the jump.
Explosively jump upwards, spreading your legs out to the sides and extending your arms overhead to form a star shape in mid-air.
Land softly with your feet together and your arms by your sides, immediately bending your knees to absorb the impact. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your leg muscles to generate the jump, avoiding excessive strain on your knees.
Ensure your knees are slightly bent as you land to absorb the impact and prevent injury.
Start with smaller jumps to perfect your form before increasing the height.
results.description: Star Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Stepmill Machine Steps
instructions: Step onto the stepmill and hold the rails lightly.
Start the machine at a comfortable speed.
Climb with full steps, pushing through your whole foot.
Keep an upright posture for the set time.
tips: Don't lean on the rails.
Increase the speed gradually.
results.description: Stepmill Machine Steps is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stepmill machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Mountain Climber
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Place your feet in the handles and assume a plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Drive your right knee towards your chest, keeping your left leg extended. Quickly switch legs, driving your left knee towards your chest while extending your right leg back.
Continue alternating legs in a running motion for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Perform the movement with a steady and controlled tempo to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Keep your shoulders directly over your hands to maintain proper alignment.
Start with a slower pace and gradually increase your speed as your strength and coordination improve.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Mountain Climber is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Triceps.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Pike
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Place your feet in the handles and assume a plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, placed directly under your shoulders, and arms slightly bent.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Keeping your legs straight, lift your hips towards the ceiling, forming an inverted V-shape with your body.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift your hips and inhale as you lower them back down.
Focus on using your core muscles to lift your hips, avoiding excessive use of your arms and legs.
Start with a smaller range of motion and gradually increase as your strength and flexibility improve.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Pike is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Tennis Forehand Ground Stroke
instructions: Stand side-on in a ready position with your knees slightly bent.
Turn your shoulders and take your hitting arm back.
Step toward the ball and rotate your hips and torso to swing forward.
Follow through across your body and return to the ready position.
tips: The power comes from rotating your hips and torso.
Stay on the balls of your feet.
results.description: Tennis Forehand Ground Stroke is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Chest, Quadriceps.

results.name: The Wall Ball
instructions: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Squat down with your chest up.
Drive up explosively and throw the ball to a target high on the wall.
Catch the ball and go straight into the next squat.
tips: Catch the ball at chest height and absorb it into the squat.
Keep your elbows under the ball.
results.description: The Wall Ball is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps, Core.

results.name: Treadmill Jogging
instructions: Stand on the treadmill with your feet on the side rails and attach the safety clip to your clothing. Start the treadmill at a low speed to safely step onto the belt.
Once you are on the moving belt, gradually increase the speed to a comfortable jogging pace, maintaining an upright posture with your core engaged.
Keep your arms bent at a 90-degree angle, swinging them naturally at your sides to match your jogging rhythm.
Maintain a steady pace, landing mid-foot with each stride and keeping your breathing steady. Jog for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Keep your head up and gaze forward, avoiding looking down at your feet.
Use a smooth, natural stride to reduce the impact on your joints.
Ensure the treadmill speed is set at a comfortable level that allows you to maintain good form.
results.description: Treadmill Jogging is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a treadmill, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Core.

results.name: Treadmill Running
instructions: Stand on the treadmill with your feet on the side rails and attach the safety clip to your clothing. Start the treadmill at a low speed to safely step onto the belt.
Once you are on the moving belt, gradually increase the speed to a running pace, maintaining an upright posture with your core engaged.
Keep your arms bent at a 90-degree angle, swinging them naturally at your sides to match your running rhythm.
Maintain a steady pace, landing mid-foot with each stride and keeping your breathing steady. Run for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Keep your head up and gaze forward, avoiding looking down at your feet.
Use a smooth, natural stride to reduce the impact on your joints.
Ensure the treadmill speed is set at a comfortable level that allows you to maintain good form.
results.description: Treadmill Running is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a treadmill, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Core.

results.name: Treadmill Walk
instructions: Step onto the treadmill and start at a slow speed.
Walk upright, looking forward, with relaxed shoulders.
Increase the speed or incline to your target effort.
Swing your arms naturally and keep a steady pace for the set time.
tips: Avoid holding the rails.
Add incline instead of speed to make walking harder.
results.description: Treadmill Walk is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a treadmill, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Tyre Flip
instructions: Squat down in front of a large tyre and grip under its edge with your chest close to it.
Drive through your legs and hips to lift the tyre.
As it rises, step forward and push it over with your hands or knee.
Reset and repeat.
tips: Lift with your legs, not your back.
Keep your arms straight during the initial lift.
results.description: Tyre Flip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a tire, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Chest, Triceps.
